Distribution Asset: Essay 18 LinkedIn Announcement

Target Canonical: https://alanpruitt.com/articles/18-the-illusion-of-the-feed.html Release Date: 2026-08-14 Strategy: Single Canonical Link (Strategy 2)

Broken links are just the visible damage. The real cost is configuration drift.

In higher education and enterprise training, it’s common practice to pull external feeds and dynamic resources directly into Learning Management Systems (LMS). But without an upstream architecture governing those assets, you aren’t just risking 404 errors—you’re silently degrading version control, audit trails, and accessibility compliance.

Newsletter Dispatch Asset: Essay 18

Subject: Architectural Debt in the LMS: Why dynamic feeds break compliance

Hey team,

Broken links in an online course are annoying, but the unseen damage is far worse: configuration drift.

When instructional designers embed external feeds or unversioned links into course modules, they introduce a point of failure that bypasses version control and audit trails. When a source changes or drops, teams spend hours manually hunting down and patching broken URLs across dozens of shells.
